chunks: 3 - Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn 'Uqdah informed us, saying: Al-Qassim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Hazim narrated to us from his book, saying: 'Ubays ibn Hisham narrated to us, from Durust ibn Abu Mansur, from al-Walid ibn Subayh, who said:

There was a conversation between me and a man called 'Abd al-Jalil regarding a succession (or appointment), so he said to me: 'Indeed, Abu 'Abdillah appointed Isma'il.' (He said) I said to Abu 'Abdillah: 'Indeed, 'Abd al-Jalil informed me that you appointed Isma'il during your lifetime, three years before your death.' He said: 'O Walid, by Allah! If I had done so, it would have been to so-and-so' (meaning Abu al-Hasan Musa) and he named him.
ai.seo_question: Did Imam al-Sadiq appoint his son Isma'il or Musa as his successor?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the critical Isma'ili dispute by contrasting a claim of prior to death with the Imam's definitive posthumous designation. It underscores the Shia principle that succession is determined by explicit *nass* (designation) rather than mere seniority or popular opinion, affirming Musa al-Kadhim as the rightful successor. The narrative serves as a primary source for distinguishing the Twelver Shia lineage from the Isma'ili branch.
